response.sql: SELECT l.ID, AVG(l.UA) AS avg_ua, AVG(l.HCT) AS avg_hct FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE RA IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(RA) <> '' AND RA <> '-') GROUP BY l.ID ORDER BY AVG(l.HCT) IS NULL, AVG(l.HCT) DESC LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: 'Recorded' means RA is non-NULL and non-empty after trimming; any other value (such as '+', '+-') counts as qualifying, and only the exact value '-' is excluded.
The qualifying test on RA is applied to a patient's records to select patients, but the averages of UA and HCT are computed over all of that patient's lab records, as the request specifies.
AVG ignores NULLs, and patients whose HCT values are all NULL get a NULL average, which the ORDER BY places last.
Ties in average HCT are not specified by the request, so their relative order is left to the database and is not deterministic.
